items.title: Stage One Unpacked: Even Mundane Purity Is Still "Easy Ground" Compared to Nirvāṇa

items.zh: 彼於戲論界易可安住，謂於世間一切種清淨；於無戲論界難可安住，謂於出世間一切種清淨。是故於彼厭惡而住，非不厭惡。
items.en: One can readily abide in the domain of conceptual elaboration — mundane purity of every kind — but can only abide with difficulty in the domain free of such elaboration — supramundane purity of every kind. One must therefore dwell in genuine revulsion towards the former; it will not do to remain without such revulsion.

items.zh: 又此住正法者，於無戲論涅槃界中，心樂安住，樂欲證得。由闕沙門果證增上力故；於己雜染相應，心生厭患；於己清淨不相應，心生厭患；於己雜染相應過患，心生厭患；於己清淨不相應過患，心生厭患；於己清淨見難成辦，心生厭患。此中略有三種雜染相應。一、未調未順而死，雜染相應。二、死已當墮煩惱大坑，雜染相應。三、由彼煩惱自在力故，現行種種惡不善業，往有怖處，雜染相應。彼觀己身闕沙門果證，由彼闕故，與三種雜染相應。如是觀已，心生厭患。當知清淨不相應亦有三種。一、諸煩惱斷究竟涅槃，名無怖處。二、能證此，謂依增上心學善心三摩地。三、能證此，於增上慧學正見所攝微妙聖道。彼觀己身，與此三種清淨不相應故，心生厭患。當知雜染相應過患，亦有三種。一、老病死苦根本之生。二、自性苦生無暇處。三、一切處生無常性。彼觀己身，有此三種雜染相應過患，心生厭患。當知清淨不相應過患有五種。一、於邊地生，未能止息。二於惡道生，未能止息。三、於在家眾諸無間業，未能偃塞。四、於出家眾無量見趣，未不相應。五、雖由世間道，乃至有頂若定、若生，而於無初後際生死流轉，未作邊際。彼觀自身，有此五種清淨不相應過患，心生厭患。於己清淨見難成辦，當知亦有五種。一、若捨不為，不能自作故。二、於所餘事非請他為能成辦故。三、決定應作故。由於自心未令清淨，必於眾苦不得解脫成吉祥性。四、非於惡業現在不作，即說彼為已作清淨，即名已得於現見法永離熾燃。無對治道，先所造作惡不善業，必不壞故。五、由彼清淨學無學道證得所顯故。彼觀清淨，由此五相難可成辦，心生厭患。又復發起堅固精進，為欲證得。彼由觀見雜染清淨，相應不相應故，心生厭患。又由觀見雜染清淨，相應不相應過患故，心生怖畏。又於清淨證得，及雜染斷滅中，有嬾惰懈怠故，心便遮止。又由作意思惟彼相故，心生厭患；即於此相多所作故，心極厭患。如厭患、極厭患，怖畏、極怖畏，遮止、極遮止，當知亦爾。

items.title: Twenty Marks of "Skilful Cultivation," and the Five Causes That Open Onto "Good Abiding"

items.zh: 如是彼以由厭俱行想，於五處所，以二十種相作意思惟故，名善修治。
items.en: Thus, applying the mind to twenty marks across five domains, joined with the perception of genuine revulsion, is called skilful cultivation.

items.zh: 復有五因，二十種相之所攝受，令於愛盡寂滅涅槃，速疾多住，心無退轉，亦無憂慮。謂我我今者為何所在。何等五因？一、由通達作意故。謂由如是通達作意無間，必能趣入正性離生，入諦現觀，證聖智見。二、由所依故。謂由依此所依無間，必能趣入正性離生，餘如前說。三、由入境界門故。謂由緣此入境界門，必能趣入正性離生，餘如前說。四、由攝受資糧故。謂由此攝受資糧，必能趣入正性離生，餘如前說。五、由攝受方便故。謂由攝受如是方便，必能趣入正性離生，乃至廣說。如是五因，當知依諦現觀逆次因說，非順次因。依最勝因，如先說事，逆次說故。

blocks.text: Why mundane purity is not enough, and how a practitioner turns towards the supramundane. The central passage is a long, searching self-examination, **untranslated** (0392c23–0393b06); the commentary summarises it.

"One can readily abide in the domain of conceptual elaboration (mundane purity), but only with difficulty in the domain free of elaboration (supramundane)." Venerable Miào Jìng: an ordinary mind settles easily in the world of false discrimination. Master Cháng Bǎi: the noble path is like eating; only one's own realisation fills one.

One who abides in the true Dharma, wishing for nirvāṇa but lacking the fruits, feels **revulsion** towards five things in oneself: - **Bound to defilement** in three ways: one may die untamed; after death fall into the pit of affliction; and under affliction's power commit evil and go to fearful places. - **Cut off from purity** in three ways: from nirvāṇa, the place without fear; from the concentration of higher mind that leads to it; from the noble path of higher wisdom. - **The dangers of defilement:** birth, the root of ageing, sickness, and death; birth in states without leisure; impermanence everywhere. - **The dangers of lacking purity:** one has not yet closed the door to rebirth in border lands or bad destinies; not yet barred the householder's heinous deeds or the renunciant's endless views; and even reaching the peak of existence, one has not ended saṃsāra. - **Purity is hard to achieve:** no one else can do it for one; it must be done; without purifying one's mind there is no freedom from suffering; merely not doing evil now does not undo past deeds without the remedy of the path; and it is achieved only through the paths of training and beyond.
Seeing this, one feels revulsion and fear, and stops laziness, and rouses firm diligence.

"Applying the mind to twenty marks across five domains, joined with the perception of genuine revulsion, is called skilful cultivation." Venerable Miào Jìng: from revulsion ("I am not pleased with myself like this") comes the resolve to change. Five causes then lead quickly to nirvāṇa without hesitation or the worry "where will I be?": penetrating attention, its basis, its gates of entry, its provisions, and its means.

quiz.q: Which domain does the treatise say is easy to abide in and which hard, and what follows?
options: mundane purity, the domain of elaboration, is easy; supramundane purity, free of it, is hard — so one must dwell in revulsion towards the former
quiz.why: "One can readily abide in the domain of conceptual elaboration — mundane purity — but only with difficulty in the domain free of elaboration — supramundane purity. One must therefore dwell in revulsion towards the former."

quiz.q: How do the two masters explain "the domain of elaboration"?
options: Miào Jìng: the world of false discrimination; Cháng Bǎi: mundane purity is conditioned, still within the domain of verbal discrimination
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the ordinary person easily abides in the domain of elaboration — the world of false discrimination, where his mind can settle. Master Cháng Bǎi: mundane purity is conditioned, still in the domain of verbal discrimination, and relatively easy to attain.

quiz.q: On seeing one's own purity as hard to accomplish, what saying does Master Cháng Bǎi use to show only oneself can achieve the path?
options: each eats and each is filled — only one's own realisation accomplishes it
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the pure noble path and nirvāṇa are like eating — each person who eats is filled; only one's own realisation can accomplish it. Venerable Miào Jìng: the path cannot be done for you by others, like hiring someone to do repentance for you.

quiz.q: What does the treatise call "skilful cultivation"?
options: applying the mind to twenty marks across five domains, joined with the perception of revulsion
quiz.why: "Thus, applying the mind to twenty marks across five domains, joined with the perception of genuine revulsion, is called skilful cultivation." Master Cháng Bǎi: the faults of association with defilement, dissociation from purity, and so on, plus the difficulty of accomplishment, make twenty marks in all.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "perception joined with revulsion"?
options: the revulsion "I am not pleased with myself like this" and perception operating together
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: from the mind of revulsion — "I am not pleased with myself like this" — revulsion and perception operate together, hence "perception joined with revulsion." He adds that present-day Buddhists fail to attain the path because their revulsion is insufficient.
